title: Confessio catholica. 2,3
shelf_note: The leaf is Johann Gerhard's Confessio catholica: a 17th-century Lutheran polemic against Bellarmine, in Latin, which matches the record. No tradition or collection is set, so there is no shelf to contradict.
structure_note: printed_backsteps 113 and printed_repeats 111 out of 859 printed numbers is high. One page cannot show the cause. Misread numerals, or 'page-num' taken from signatures, are more likely than a broken scan order, but the book should get a catchword check. The structure count gives pages_translated 0, but the book field gives 581: one of the two counts is wrong (E2).

missing.why: the Greek word (hypōpiazō, 1 Cor 9:27) is lost, and nothing says it is the word Paul uses, so the argument about its meaning cannot be followed
'satisfactory' is the technical term for works that make satisfaction (temporal penalty paid for sin), not the everyday sense of the word
Pierre Coton, the Jesuit, and his Institution catholique are not identified; a reader cannot tell who is being answered

book_verdict: A clean 17th-century print with good OCR and a faithful translation. The only things a reader meets are the Greek 'Ἔκθεσις' turned into 'Exthesis' (and footnoted as the original) and a Greek word replaced by an English gloss. Nothing is serious.
